cues.text: Good morning. I’ve been looking at your holidays to Australia in your brochure. I’m thinking of going during the second half of next month.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Good morning. As you can see from our brochure, we oﬀer a wide variety of packages to various destinations in Australia. Is there anything in particular that interests you?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yes, my husband and I are very interested in the holidays in the Outback.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: These holidays are becoming increasingly popular. Would you like to arrange flights and accommodation with us, or just accommodation?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Can you arrange flights from Sydney?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Certainly.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: OK, flight and accommodation then.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Right. You said that you wanted to travel next month. Which date would you prefer? I should point out that there are no daily ﬂights available, so if you have a flexible itinerary, that’s better.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Well, we arrive in Sydney on the 15th of April and we were thinking of travelling to the Outback on the 18th of August, er... I mean April.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: OK. There’s only one ﬂight from Sydney to Alice Springs on the 18th, so I’ll book you on that. It leaves at 10 in the morning, which is quite convenient. Shall I book two seats for you?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yes, please.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: As for your stay in the Outback, you can see from the brochure that we oﬀer three packages - budget, standard, and luxury. The budget package is about 500 Australian dollars. The standard package is about 700 and the luxury one is approximately 1,000, though it does depend on exactly what you would like regarding extras. Which one would you prefer?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Well, we can’t decide between the budget and standard options.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Ah, well, actually, just looking at my computer here, on the date that you want to ﬂy into Alice Springs, there is no standard accommodation available. It’s fully booked, I’m afraid.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: That’s OK. We think that the cheapest one should be ﬁne for us. We don’t mind roughing it for a few days and we don’t expect to be spending much time at the accommodation. We prefer the outdoors.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Right. Let’s look at the room options.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: First of all, would you prefer a non smoking room?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yes. Neither of us smokes.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: OK.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Oh, before I forget, could you book everything in my husband's name, please?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Yes, of course. Are you paying by credit card?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yes.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: In that case, I’ll need your husband’s name exactly as it appears on the card.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Of course. It’s John A. Smyth. That’s Smyth with a “Y”.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: John ... middle initial “A”... surname Smyth, S-M-Y-T-H. Is that correct?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Correct.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Thank you. I’ll just check the price. The room will cost 100 dollars a night plus 10 dollars tax, so 110 dollars per night in total. Is that OK?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yes, that’s fine. Book us for three nights, please.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Most of the guests like to participate in some special activities and trips while they are staying in the Outback. Is there anything that interests you and your husband?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yes, there are several things we’d like to see and do. We’d deﬁnitely like to visit the Cultural Centre.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Yes, that’s very popular. It’s within walking distance of the accommodation and it’s free. It’s also a great place to pick up souvenirs of your trip.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: We were thinking about visiting one of the nearby farms.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: There are two farms nearby - a sheep farm and a kangaroo farm. There is also an opportunity to ride camels in the desert. Have you ridden a camel before?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: No, but it sounds like fun. Could you give me some more details about the kangaroo farm and the camel ride?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Certainly. The kangaroo farm includes information on how the animals are raised whilst the camel ride provides information on desert ﬂora and fauna. Which would you prefer? You can arrange to see the kangaroos in the wild if you like, rather than on a farm.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: That sounds perfect. OK, we’ll go on the camel ride and see the kangaroos in their natural habitat.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: OK. I’ll arrange that for you. I forgot to mention that the journey also includes a stop at a place of aboriginal artwork. It’s a place well-known for its stone carvings of animals and mythical creatures.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: That sounds great! Are the carvings in the desert?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Yes.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Wonderful!
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Well, that’s perfect then. I’m sure you'll have a lovely trip, but remember that you need take care in the sun.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yes. We’re really looking forward to our trip. We really want to try to experience the Dreamtime under the stars.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Of course. That’s what a trip to the Outback is really all about.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yes. Now, how about the cost...
cues.speaker: Woman
